Good morning, friends. **Prem** here. Wishing a Happy Diwali to all of you,
including **[Vivek Ramaswamy](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfTzZAADUIa/)**
😊.

In today's **' First Draft,'** we make the definitive case for **Chris Van
Hollen** to replace **Chuck Schumer** as Senate majority leader, liberal think
tank chief **Neera Tanden** urges activists not to ask the forthcoming
Democratic-controlled Congress for anything special, and **Pete Hegseth**
could be impeached this week. And a little housekeeping note: there will be no
**' First Draft'** on Wednesday, but we'll be back in your inbox on Thursday!

# Fight Club

Stephen Maturen/Getty Images._

In the weeks leading up to the New York City mayoral election, Chris Van
Hollen was angry.

Zohran Mamdani, a 33-year-old democratic socialist, just upended U.S.
politics, winning the Democratic primary and becoming the nominee to lead the
biggest city in the country.

While Mamdani was impressing voters, many Democratic officials refused to
endorse him, or continued to implicitly or explicitly undermine him. Van
Hollen, who endorsed Mamdani in September, slammed them for remaining mum.

**" Many Democratic members of the Senate and the House delegations
representing New York have stayed on the sidelines,"** he
[said](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/13/us/politics/van-hollen-zohran-
mamdani.html). **" That kind of spineless politics is what people are sick
of."**

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

The race, of course, was between Mamdani; Curtis Sliwa, the Republican; and
Andrew Cuomo, an alleged sexual abuser funded by Trump-allied billionaires who
lost the primary and decided to run as an independent.

One of the New York pols keeping silent was Chuck Schumer, Democrats' pro-
Israel Senate minority leader, who refused to say whom he was supporting in
the race - and never ended up endorsing.

A year later, Democrats have secured a significant Senate majority, fueled in
part by candidates across the country adopting the same messaging focus on
"affordability" as Mamdani.

Who will that majority choose to lead them now? The senator who rallied behind
a mayor who's changed the American political landscape, who has led by
example, traveling to El Salvador and Palestine to confront abuses by Trump
and Israel? Or the party's current Senate leader, who has again and again
bailed out Republicans, sacrificed Democrats' upper hand, done little to slow
Trump's immigration terror machine, and unconditionally supported Israel's
genocidal U.S. tax-funded violence?

No challenger to Schumer has emerged yet, even as his approval ratings
[continue to fall](https://www.realclearpolling.com/polls/favorability/chuck-
schumer). Still, a number of Democrats have expressed interest in new
leadership, or remain uncommitted to supporting Schumer, including:

  * [Richard Blumenthal (Conn.)](https://x.com/johncraven1/status/2119818026698830213?a=H94BrYsS6T-nbFEPiLw&s=20)

  * [Chris Van Hollen (Md.)](https://www.fox5dc.com/news/maryland-sen-van-hollen-eyes-2028-presidential-bid-declines-endorse-schumer-senate-majority-leader)

  * [Ed Markey (Mass.)](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/11/06/newsletters/markey-senate-leader-schumer-the-scrum/)

  * [Bernie Sanders (Vt.)](https://www.newsweek.com/chuck-schumer-favorites-replace-democratic-senate-leader-12656990)

  * [Elizabeth Warren (Mass.)](https://www.newsweek.com/chuck-schumer-favorites-replace-democratic-senate-leader-12656990)

  * [Elissa Slotkin (Mich.)](https://x.com/PamphletsY/status/2118457619891540240?a=fDZiD4Z0zCd_3O0mrQ4&s=20)

  * [Annie Andrews (S.C.)](https://x.com/keithedwards/status/2118526818571714791?a=_Zs8_0B4YCW0pjbn0bg&s=20)

  * [Abdul El-Sayed (Mich.)](https://truthout.org/articles/el-sayed-backs-van-hollen-for-senate-leader-as-calls-to-replace-schumer-grow/)

  * [Peggy Flanagan (Minn.)](https://x.com/PamphletsY/status/2118355912431649037?a=jkfSDm34Wf92XFVEJkU&s=20)

  * [Adam Hamilton (Kan.)](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/4/kansas-elects-democrat-adam-hamilton)

  * [Troy Jackson (Maine)](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/4/democrat-troy-jackson-wins-maine-us-senate-seat-in-blow-to-republicans)

  * [Chris Pappas (N.H.)](https://x.com/PamphletsY/status/2118478941275009381?a=OsIpbFkbfRSVdYfE6wQ&s=20)

  * [Julianna Stratton (Ill.)](https://x.com/PamphletsY/status/2118358837199790098?a=jDNX1Xet0l4DfhxY1Vk&s=20)

  * [James Talarico (Tex.)](https://x.com/PamphletsY/status/2118432234269266215?a=SgyRvyGxfytBhdEtLsw&s=20)

On Monday evening, Michigan Senator Elissa Slotkin, a moderate whom
[some](https://x.com/PodSaveAmerica/status/2119155591864345000?a=AvBZnU_cjN35yKWpiJ4&s=20)
have advanced as a possible new Senate leader,
[met](https://x.com/alanhe/status/2119915246525595962?a=hFpGkC89mR7FZk552NM&s=20)
with Van Hollen and **" had a great conversation,"** which she'd **" have more
to say about… later."**

Immediately afterward, she
[told](https://x.com/BenjaminSWeiss/status/2119938309078315060) reporters
she's currently withholding her vote for leader. **" I think the country made
clear that they want a new generation of leadership with big and bold
ideas,"** Slotkin said, adding that **" at a minimum anyone who wants to be
majority leader should lay out what they're going to do differently and what
their plan is to help the American people, especially in the first 100
days."**

It's a reasonable ask. As **Zeteo** [pointed
out](https://zeteo.com/p/democrats-affordability-agenda) Monday, while
Democrats campaigned on "affordability" in the midterms, it's not clear what
their agenda is for making life more affordable than it was in 2024, when Dems
again lost again to Donald Trump - nor is it clear that they'd give themselves
an opportunity to pass it by finally ending the filibuster.

Schumer, as leader, is subjected sometimes to inordinate levels of criticism
from all sides. But in several high-profile moments throughout the Trump-Vance
administration, where Van Hollen leaned in, Schumer appeared to lean away - or
failed to marshal his caucus productively.

Throughout his career, including as leader, Schumer has always seemed to play
into corporate America's so-called **["rotating
villain"](https://www.salon.com/2010/02/23/democrats_34/)** strategy, in which
there are always just enough dissenting Democrats to hamstring progressive
parts of the Democratic agenda, and the party typically fails to match
Republican legislative tactics in kind.

Early on in the administration, a quarter of Schumer's caucus voted with
Republicans to pass the [Laken Riley Act](https://zeteo.com/p/why-democrats-
voting-gop-immigration-bill-laken-riley) - a bill that enabled Trump's ICE to
throw immigrants in detention without due process. It helped give legitimacy
to Trump's immigration policies - and the horrors that followed.

Schumer has often failed to force concessions from Republicans in government-
funding fights, including last November, when Democrats allowed Republicans to
reopen the government without getting them to reauthorize subsidies that
helped millions of Americans buy health insurance.

Then, in February of this year, Republicans and Democrats clashed over funding
the Department of Homeland Security, after federal agents murdered Renee
Nicole Good and Alex Pretti amid the administration's
[invasion](https://zeteo.com/p/watch-inside-trumps-war-on-minneapolis-ice-
trump-murder-shooting-immigrants) of Minnesota. The partial shutdown was the
longest ever - 75 days. Democrats didn't completely lose here - but they also
didn't secure meaningful changes at DHS.

All the while, Schumer has maintained support for Israel. The man who once
[said](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/03/18/opinion/schumer-trump-
antisemitism.html) **" my job is to keep the left pro-Israel"** has
[opposed](https://www.democrats.senate.gov/news/press-releases/leader-schumer-
statement-on-the-resolutions-of-disapproval-on-aid-to-
israel?utm_source=chatgpt.com) blocking weapon sales to Israel and - while
occasionally writing strongly-worded letters - has not come out in favor of
using any actual leverage to force Israel to stop violating human rights.

[Share](https://zeteo.com/p/run-chris-
run?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&action=share)

Schumer has operated specifically against the will of Democrats' voter base -
which has become overwhelmingly critical of Israel, supports abolishing ICE,
and is eager for leaders to confront power.

Trump said nice-ish things about Schumer this week. He predicted the Democrat
would probably secure the role as majority leader,
[saying](https://x.com/clashreport/status/2118453744233041928?a=h69g09dCFz5P3BnqlEE&s=20)
**" he's actually not a bad guy. I know him, I know him very well, I know him
better than most."**

In this context, calls within the party are increasing for new leadership -
some of which specify Van Hollen as a desired replacement. While Van Hollen
initially rejected the idea of challenging Schumer, he
[said](https://x.com/alanhe/status/2119924855630102613?a=8h_1D8LNbig1u8ghRxk&s=20)
Monday he is now **" in listening mode."**

Van Hollen's instincts and leadership on endorsing Mamdani are emblematic of
the broader case for him to be leader.

He has both honored public opinion, _and_ sought to move it; both exercises
which party leadership has been resistant to do. On issues like Medicare for
All, Van Hollen - once a member of House Speaker Nancy Pelosi's leadership
team - has [come around](https://portside.org/2025-12-03/we-must-stop-
tinkering-around-edges-van-hollen-makes-case-medicare-all-amid-aca-fight) to
support the increasingly popular policy.

Meanwhile, the Maryland senator has taken it upon himself to move public
opinion on issues that were either presumed by the media and political
establishment to be Republicans' signature issue, or issues that wouldn't
influence voters.

After the Trump administration shipped hundreds of immigrants without due
process to the notorious CECOT megaprison in El Salvador, Van Hollen went to
El Salvador himself and demanded to see one of the victims, his unlawfully
deported constituent Kilmar Abrego Garcia - not taking "no" for an answer.

Van Hollen's trip set off a chain of events. First, he proved Abrego Garcia
was alive, meeting with him. Other Democratic lawmakers traveled to CECOT
seeking answers.

All the while, public sentiment on Trump's handling of immigration
[tanked](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trumps-immigration-approval-drops-
record-low-reutersipsos-poll-finds-2026-01-26/). An issue Republicans had a
substantial net-positive rating on became an albatross. In June, as Trump's
approval continued to tank, the government finally gave in to the courts and
brought Abrego Garcia back. While he still faces vindictive legal efforts from
Trump, the Maryland father is back home.

Due in part to Van Hollen, a dad is home with his wife and kids - and
Republicans' signature fall-back issue is now deflated.

Van Hollen has brought that same spirit to foreign policy. Not only has he
been a leading critic of the unconditional U.S.-Israel relationship and led
votes to block weapons to Israel - Van Hollen physically went to Palestine.

In August, Oregon Senator Jeff Merkley journeyed with Van Hollen to the
Israeli-occupied West Bank. There, the pair spotlighted escalating Israeli
violence against both Palestinians and Americans.

Van Hollen was also part of the internal Senate ["Fight
Club"](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/24/us/politics/schumer-democrats-
senate-fight-club.html) - alongside Senators Tina Smith, Chris Murphy, Bernie
Sanders, Elizabeth Warren, Ed Markey, Jeff Merkley, and Martin Heinrich -
supporting successful primary challenges to corporate-friendly candidates
recruited by Schumer and DSCC chair Senator Kirsten Gillibrand.

Before this week, Van Hollen has maintained he's ['kicking the
tires"](https://zeteo.com/p/is-chris-van-hollen-running-for-president) on a
2028 presidential campaign, a prospect that's also excited many progressives.
To be fair, no one said a majority leader couldn't run for president, too.

Majority Leader Lyndon B. Johnson ran for the 1960 Democratic nomination.
While he fell short, he became John F. Kennedy's running mate on a successful
ticket. He, of course, became president after Kennedy's assassination, and
then won his own 1964 election in a landslide.

In any case - whether for Senate leader, or the presidency, or both: Run,
Chris, run!

## 🇮🇷 Iran War Updates

  * **' Effectively over':** Trump [said](https://zeteo.com/p/didnt-even-try-how-chuck-schumer) yesterday that he believes the war with Iran "militarily is effectively over…We're just keeping it the status quo." The comments came after his meeting with Qatar's prime minister, which [reportedly](https://aje.news/84oq18?update=5137638) produced no major breakthroughs.

  * **Falling prices:** Still, amid cautious but growing hope that the war may soon end, Brent crude futures[ briefly dropped below $90 a barrel](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/oil-falls-trump-downplays-prospect-escalation-with-iran-2026-11-10/) for the first time since August earlier today. 

  * **Impeachment watch:** Outgoing Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) [reintroduced](https://x.com/acyn/status/2119869529773969858?s=46) eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, for waging Trump's illegal war in Iran, failing to minimize civilian casualties, and more. Hegseth [said](https://x.com/MaryMargOlohan/status/2119842342547157054) he'll hold a press conference at the Pentagon today. Trump [said](https://x.com/atrupar/status/2119915666698371575?s=46), "I'll stand by him." There could be an impeachment vote this week. 

  * **Wider war:** Yemen's Houthi rebels said the Saudi-led coalition conducted airstrikes on several places in the capital, Sanaa, today, while Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted two missiles and a drone fired by the Houthis toward the kingdom, Al Jazeera [reported](https://aje.news/1peed1?update=5138258). Meanwhile, Israel [continued](https://aje.news/1peed1?update=5138458) attacking parts of southern Lebanon in violation of the so-called ceasefire there.

## 'Not a Time to Pressure Congress'

Now that Democrats have won significant majorities in Congress, liberal
influencer and Center for American Progress president Neera Tanden headed to
the National Press Club to offer "some friendly advice" to people who might
want Democrats to support progressive policy ideas: Shut up. Shut up. Shut up.
Really.

"The next two years should not be an opportunity for every organization or
group in DC to dust off their wishlist for the last decade," Tanden laughed.
"It's not a time to pressure Congress to fruitlessly spend time, political
capital on ideas that we couldn't get done in a Democratic trifecta just a few
years ago."

A former Joe Biden aide, Tanden leads Democrats' preeminent Washington policy
think tank. Apparently, she also gets to decide whether Americans can make
policy demands of their elected representatives.

## **🗞 ️ **What You Need to Know

  * **Ready for AOC:** Progressives are [seeking](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/11/09/progressives-launch-effort-draft-aoc-run-president/) to gather a million signatures urging New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to run for president.

  * **Enough, Chuck:** The 600,000-member Machinists Union urged Chuck Schumer not to run for Senate majority leader, [calling](https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2026/11/09/congress/union-sours-on-schumer-01157983) for a "new generation of leadership."

  * **Counting votes:** Democrat Scott Colom now [holds](https://www.wlbt.com/2026/11/09/colom-leads-hyde-smith-by-more-than-2500-votes-mississippi-awaits-final-senate-result/) a 2,500-vote lead over Mississippi GOP Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith. Democrat Mary Peltola [has](https://alaskabeacon.com/2026/11/09/peltola-extends-lead-over-sullivan-in-alaskas-u-s-senate-race-as-ballot-counting-continues/) a 2,500-vote lead over Alaska GOP Senator Dan Sullivan, though that race is expected to go to a ranked-choice runoff. Democrat Eileen Laubacher was [projected](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/09/politics/lauren-boebert-lose-reelection-eileen-laubacher) to defeat far-right Rep. Lauren Boebert. AP [reported](https://apnews.com/article/california-billionaire-tax-4ae8cbdc057b99579818016f02ac9d9e) California voters had rejected a new tax on billionaires - Proposition 40 - after a divisive campaign that saw billionaires spend hundreds of millions of dollars to [defeat the measure](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/09/california-tax-billionaires-prop-40). 

  * **Lame duck action:** Senators voted 73-25 to advance permitting legislation in the lame duck session, after Al Gore [said](https://x.com/algore/status/2119859815593742773) it would be "an extremely serious mistake" and "do far more harm than good." Trump, meanwhile, [said](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/09/trump-says-he-will-not-approve-wind-permits-as-part-of-permitting-bill-01157629) the bill "hasn't been fully negotiated," and that he won't approve wind turbines.

  * **Getting to business:** Trump's new chief of staff, ghoulish fascist Stephen Miller, will [no longer recuse](https://www.theatlantic.com/politics/2026/11/stephen-miller-katie-ai-stock/689356/) himself from matters involving AI and Elon Musk's SpaceX after his wife ended her work with the company and sold her SpaceX stock.

  * **Greener pastures:** Dirt farmer and former Senator Jon Tester (D-Mont.) is [advising](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/09/nx-s1-6029641/palantir-congress-jon-tester-investigations) ICE-involved spy tech firm Palantir. Texas Lieutenant Governor Dan Patrick, who lost in the GOP midterm bloodbath, is still in office, but that didn't stop him from [launching](https://www.chron.com/politics/article/dan-patrick-texas-next-move-22521504.php) a "strategic consulting" website [bragging](https://patrickstrategies.us/) about how he "knows where the money is."

## 🌏 Anywhere But America

  * **🇵 🇸 Don't forget Gaza: **Palestinian media [reported](https://english.wafa.ps/Pages/Details/176800) that at least three people were injured yesterday after a residential building wall fell on a nearby tent, as heavy rain, strong winds, and falling temperatures worsen the already horrific and unsafe conditions Palestinians live in due to Israel's genocide. Hundreds of thousands of Palestinians are now living in open-air conditions due to mass flooding of tents housing forcibly displaced people, officials told WAFA. 

  * **🇬 🇧 Sexual predator sentenced: **British comedian and MAGA influencer [Russell Brand](https://zeteo.com/p/maga-influencer-russell-brand-convicted) was [sentenced](https://www.bbc.com/news/live/c670ppzjwxpnt) to 10 and a half years in prison after being convicted of rape and sexual assault. The judge called him a "sexual predator" with "arrogant disregard of any woman's right to say no." He is under investigation for two additional rape allegations, police [said](https://www.theguardian.com/culture/2026/nov/05/russell-brand-detective-other-potential-victims) last week.

  * **🇵 🇱 Gunman dies:** The 24-year-old gunman who killed six people in central Krakow, Poland, on Saturday has died in the hospital, authorities said yesterday, after police shot him during the attack. Police are still investigating the motive of the attacker, [identified](https://apnews.com/article/poland-krakow-shooting-489bc2e25a2684b96b59682d0faee3e8) as Michał Oksiński. Read more from **Zeteo UK** [here](https://zeteo.uk/p/polish-politicians-shouldnt-be-pointing).

  * 🇦🇷 **Popular pope:** An estimated 2.5 million people [flocked](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/huge-crowds-gather-buenos-aires-pope-leos-outdoor-mass-2026-11-09/) to Argentina's capital, Buenos Aires, yesterday for a mass led by Pope Leo XIV. It was the largest crowd of his papacy so far. During his visit, Leo spoke about the importance and dignity of workers, people living with disabilities, and the world's poorest. His comments were widely [viewed](https://apnews.com/article/pope-argentina-milei-labor-unemployment-disabilities-2ad4ba74d0cff90fb49569df400ac582) as a rebuke of far-right Argentine President Javier Milei.
